title: Recursive chain-map identity and uniform coordinate formula
statement: Let G be a group, H a subgroup, n≥1, and a:Fin(n+1)→G. Use B, J, P, chosen vertices and diagonal H actions defined in [def-sfb-ordered-join-coset-chains]. Then dP_q=P_{q-1}d for 0≤q≤n. For each 0≤q≤n there exists a finite list of integers c and degree-q symbols over the constant family Fin(q+1), independent of all inputs h:Fin(q+1)→H, whose evaluation by sending color i and coordinate index j to h_j a_i is P_q[h_0,...,h_q]. Repeated terms may be retained. This states only the recursive comparison properties, without erasure or the composite map.

proof.text: For $B_\bullet(Y)$ the boundary has square zero. Indeed, when original positions $a<b$ are deleted, deleting $a$ first and then position $b-1$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b-1}$, while deleting $b$ first and then position $a$ contributes $(-1)^{a+b}$. The resulting ordered tuples agree and the coefficients cancel. This pairs all terms, even when tuple entries coincide. At degree one the resulting tuple is the empty tuple; at degrees zero and $-1$ the second boundary is zero by definition. Deletion commutes with diagonal left translation because it removes the same position before or after translation; augmentation commutes because its target has trivial action.

proof.text: Start the chain-map induction with $dP_0[h]=d[(0,ha_0)]=1=P_{-1}d[h]$. The augmented identity in degree $-1$ is $0=0$. Suppose $1\leq q\leq n$ and the identities in smaller degrees are known. For $x=[h_0,\ldots,h_q]$ put $z=P_{q-1}(dx)$. Then $dz=P_{q-2}(d^2x)=0$ (for $q=1$ use the degree-zero identity and $P_{-1}=1$). The contraction identity of [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction] in degree $q-1$ reads $dS^{h_0}_{q-1}z+S^{h_0}_{q-2}dz=z$, since $0\leq q-1\leq n-1=r-2$. Therefore $dP_qx=z=P_{q-1}dx$. Extend additively. This proves the induction without using any contraction identity in the top degree $n$.

proof.text: Construct the finite lists inductively as formal lists, without collecting equal terms. For $q=0$ take the single term with coefficient $1$, color $0$ and index $0$. Suppose the list in degree $q-1$ is fixed. For each deleted position $t\in\{0,\ldots,q\}$, let $\rho_t:\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,q\}$ be the increasing inclusion missing $t$. Copy that list, multiply each coefficient by $(-1)^t$, and replace each coordinate index $j$ by $\rho_t(j)$. Concatenation is the expansion of $P_{q-1}(d[h_0,\ldots,h_q])$. For each term apply the finite insertion/replacement expansion of $S^{h_0}$ in [lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction]. Keep the coordinate indices of retained vertices, and assign index $0$ to each inserted or replaced chosen vertex, since it is $h_0a_i$. Multiply the integer coefficients and concatenate all lists. The cited expansion depends only on the color list and $r$, so the resulting finite coefficients, colors and indices depend only on $q,n$. Each resulting symbol has $q+1$ increasing colors and all indices lie in $\{0,\ldots,q\}$. This proves the required formula for all inputs, including equal coordinates and coincident cosets; cancellations need never be detected.

theorem cosetComparisonRecursion (H : Subgroup G) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (a : Fin (n + 1) → G) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ n →
      (boundary (Coset H a) (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q)).comp (comparison H a (q + 1)) =
        (comparison H a q).comp (tupleBoundary H (q : ℤ) (arityDegree q))) ∧
    (∀ q : ℕ, q ≤ n →
      ∃ L : List (ℤ × Symbol (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Fin (q + 1)) (q : ℤ)),
        ∀ h : Fin (q + 1) → H,
          comparison H a (q + 1) (tupleTerm (q : ℤ) (List.ofFn h)) =
            (L.map (fun t ↦ t.1 •
              chainMap (fun i j ↦ vertex H a (h j) i) (q : ℤ)
                (Finsupp.single t.2 1))).sum)
